data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues separation is unnecessary under information-theoretic blindness, but restricting the checker to the final claim only does not address the problem's core concern: the same engine's shared training priors. A checker reconstructing a proof from first principles still samples from the same P(Output|Prompt) with the same blind spots as the author. Its own countercondition—shared priors so dominant that any two paths are identical—directly admits this failure mode it never refutes, so the independence it claims is not genuine.
